segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ מִנְחַת יִשְׂרָאֵל – קוֹפֵל אֶחָד לִשְׁנַיִם, וּשְׁנַיִם לְאַרְבָּעָה, וּמַבְדִּיל. מִנְחַת כֹּהֲנִים – קוֹפֵל אֶחָד לִשְׁנַיִם, וּשְׁנַיִם לְאַרְבָּעָה, וְאֵינוֹ מַבְדִּיל. מִנְחַת כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ – לֹא הָיָה מְקַפְּלָה. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מִנְחַת כֹּהֲנִים וּמִנְחַת כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ אֵין בָּהֶן פְּתִיתָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן קְמִיצָה, וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן קְמִיצָה – אֵין בָּהֶן פְּתִיתָה. וְכוּלָּן פּוֹתְתָן כְּזֵיתִים.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In breaking «the meal offering of an Israelite» into pieces, the priest «folds [kofel] one» into two «and two into four and separates» it at the folds. In breaking into pieces «the meal offering of priests,» the priest «folds one into two and two into four and does not separate» it at the folds. Because no handful is removed, separation is unnecessary. In the case of the griddle-cake «meal offering of the anointed priest, he would not fold it. Rabbi Shimon says:» In neither «the meal offering of priests nor the meal offering of the anointed priest is there breaking» into pieces, «because in» those meal offerings «there is no removal of a handful. And any» meal offering «in which there is no removal of a handful there is no breaking» into pieces. «And» in «all» meal offerings that are broken into pieces, the priest «breaks them» into «olive-bulk-»sized pieces.
